title: All module sheaves on a discrete algebraic scheme are locally constant
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, and $p:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose the underlying topology of Z is discrete. Every etale sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on Z is locally constant [def-constructible-locally-constant]. Z and the modules need not be finite.

proof.text: Cover Z by its open singletons T. For its unique point t, Spec kappa(t) -> T is a closed immersion and is surjective, hence a universal homeomorphism. Its residue field is isomorphic to k by the Nullstellensatz because t is closed and T is locally of finite type over k.

Every set sheaf on Spec kappa(t) has invertible constant-sheaf counit. The constant-sheaf comparison with forgetting module structure identifies the forgotten module counit with that counit composed with an isomorphism. Since forgetting module structure reflects isomorphisms, the module counit is invertible too. Thus any module sheaf on that spectrum is constant.

Apply the preceding assertion to the pullback of F|T to Spec kappa(t). Constant sheaves are locally constant, and universal-homeomorphism descent gives local constancy on T. Local constancy is etale local, so compose the singleton open cover and its trivializations to prove local constancy on Z. This includes the empty scheme and requires neither a finite cover nor finite generation of modules.
